doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

chapter: The Bay Area scene and tastes
title: Opinion of smooth jazz
summary: He prefers acoustic instruments and tunes with changes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What’s your opinion of smooth jazz?

Well I don’t know where they got the name. It’s like sometimes we play, you know you play somewhere and you’re playing and it’s like it’s got this kind of seamless, flawless quality to it. And you might be playing someplace and it might be — I mean as jazz musicians we work, I mean I play weddings, I play — but I play the way I play, I’m not going to play — if you want funk or this or that then you get those guys, you don’t get me. Sometimes we play and it’s like real sort of subdued and quiet. After the tune’s over I’ll look at the guys and I said, “If this ain’t smooth jazz I’ll kiss your ass.” So I don’t know. It’s a style of music. I like hearing tunes and chord changes and things like, that’s all. I mean I suppose if I grew up in a different time I could be doing that. I think about the kids, when I deal with kids, I see kids with spiked hair and they’ve got everything going for them and I think well if I was 16 that’s probably where I’d be. Right? I mean how can you not look at it that way. So I feel that way about styles of music. But it’s not for me. Like I said I like acoustic instruments. It seems to me that smooth jazz or whatever that type of music is is mostly electric bass, electric keyboards. I like acoustic sounding instruments. So leave it there.
